claim_verdicts.evidence: `git show stage-1:DonHang.Infrastructure/LoggingNotifier.cs` lines 9-13 are character-for-character the lesson's block: `public sealed class LoggingNotifier(ILogger<LoggingNotifier> logger) : INotifier` / `public void Send(int orderId, string subject) => logger.LogInformation("notification for order {OrderId}: {Subject}", orderId, subject);`. One template, two named placeholders ({OrderId}, {Subject}), two arguments after the template. Lines 6-8 skipped by the block are the `// lesson: design.l1.solid-dip` comment only.

`git show stage-1:DonHang.Api/Middleware/RequestLoggingMiddleware.cs` lines 9-24 match the lesson's block verbatim, including the call `logger.LogInformation("{Method} {Path} responded {StatusCode} in {ElapsedMs}ms", context.Request.Method, context.Request.Path, context.Response.StatusCode, stopwatch.ElapsedMilliseconds);`. Four placeholders, four arguments, in that order. Lines 5-8 skipped by the block are the comment naming backend.l1.middleware-pipeline and this lesson as reusers.

Logging overview, "Log message template": "Each log API uses a message template. The message template can contain placeholders for which arguments are provided." and "This approach lets logging providers implement semantic or structured logging. The arguments themselves are passed to the logging system, not just the formatted message template. This enables logging providers to store the parameter values as fields." Earlier: "The key name (or placeholder) comes from the word inside the curly braces in the template, and the value comes from the remaining method argument."

Ran live 2026-09-25: POST /api/v1/auth/login then POST /api/v1/orders against the running lab returned `201 Created`, `Location: .../api/v1/orders/26`. `docker logs donhang-api --since 3m` then printed, plain text and not JSON: "info: DonHang.Infrastructure.LoggingNotifier[0]" / "      notification for order 26: order placed" and "info: DonHang.Api.Middleware.RequestLoggingMiddleware[0]" / "      POST /api/v1/orders responded 201 in 13ms".
claim_verdicts.source: live: docker logs donhang-api --since 3m, examples/don-hang lab running at localhost:8080

claim_verdicts.evidence: True for this call, too strong in general. C# reference: "If an interpolated string has the type `string`, the compiler typically transforms it into a String.Format method call." But also: "The compiler checks if an interpolated string is assigned to a type that satisfies the interpolated string handler pattern" — a method whose parameter is a handler type does receive the pieces separately. `LogInformation(string? message, params object?[] args)` takes `string`, so there the value is finished first.
claim_verdicts.suggested_text: When an interpolated string is passed to a parameter of type `string` — as `LogInformation(string? message, params object?[] args)` is — the compiler finishes it into one `string` (typically via `String.Format`) before the call, so the method never sees the placeholder names or the values separately. (C# 10+ interpolated string handler parameters are the exception; `ILogger` has none.)

issues.text: The fill answer set `["{OrderId}"]` is incomplete relative to the prompt. The prompt asks for "the placeholder name", and the .NET docs call the name the word inside the braces ("The key name (or placeholder) comes from the word inside the curly braces"), so `OrderId` is the literal answer to the question asked, while the blank's position inside the template string requires `{OrderId}`. Both spellings are defensible; only one is accepted.
issues.fix: Either add `OrderId` to `answer` (making it `["{OrderId}", "OrderId"]`), or change the prompt to "fill in the placeholder, braces included, that makes `orderId` its own field" so only `{OrderId}` can be intended.
issues.quote: fill in the placeholder name that makes `orderId` its own field

issues.fix: Add one clause to "How it works" after "the value itself arrives as a separate argument": "matched to its placeholder by position, not by name". issues.text: The explanation for distractor c dismisses a performance difference as if none existed. The .NET docs say the opposite direction is real: "In most cases, you should use log message template formatting when logging. Use of string interpolation can cause performance issues." The key (a) is still uniquely correct — c misnames "the real problem" — but the explanation teaches something the docs contradict.
issues.fix: Reword c's explanation to: "There is a cost difference — the docs recommend templates over interpolation partly for performance — but that is not what this review missed: the change removed a named field, and the console test could never have shown it."
issues.quote: the lesson never claims one template is faster than the other

issues.text: "independently searchable" is stated without the condition the docs attach to it. The docs frame field storage as a provider capability: "This enables logging providers to store the parameter values as fields" — and this app's console provider does not let you filter by `OrderId` at all. Section 4 hedges correctly ("for anything built to read the event"); the Core concepts definition does not, and a reader meets the unconditional version first.
issues.fix: Change the bullet to: "field — one named value inside a structured log line, searchable on its own by any provider that stores the fields, unlike a substring buried inside free text."
